source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Press UID manually
2. Check the behavior and color of UID
3. Login BMC web press UID on.
4. Check the behavior and color of UID
5. Login BMC web press UID off.
6. Check the behavior and color of UID
7. Login BMC web and remote KVM.
8. Use ipmitool command light UID : ipmitool chassis identify
9. Check the behavior and color of UID

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Physical and WebUI UID LED should be bright Blue when turning on manually
2. Physical and WebUI UID LED should be OFF when turning off manually
3. Physical and WebUI UID LED should be bright Blue when turning on by BMC web control.
4. Physical and WebUI UID LED should be OFF when turning on BMC web control.
5. Physical and WebUI UID should be flashing when user remote the system.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO captures the visual boundary but ignores that WebUI and IPMI control are partly automatable, does not examine the contradictory WebUI-on Criteria, and omits the KVM-versus-identify flash trigger ambiguity.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED correctly identifies the opposite expected states for WebUI UID-on and requires a corrected state/control matrix, chassis identity, bounded identify behavior, visual evidence and final restore.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 812/2291 repeats NO despite quoting both contradictory WebUI-on Criteria; it does not reconcile the control paths or define which action owns the flashing state.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-977 draft was inspected only as history. This review independently adds the second causal ambiguity created by opening remote KVM and then issuing `chassis identify` before a single observation checkpoint.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 requires preserved source plus an explicit engineering correction rather than silently fixing Criteria 4; ED-36 allows readiness inputs but not irreconcilable core acceptance; ED-38 keeps physical actions, remote control and DUT verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Validate synchronization of the physical chassis UID indicator and WebUI representation across four intended control contexts: physical-button on/off, BMC WebUI on/off, remote KVM context and IPMI chassis-identify behavior, including steady blue, off and flashing indications. The Master does not currently provide a self-consistent action-to-state mapping.
original_method: An operator presses the physical UID control and observes physical/WebUI state; an authorized user then operates WebUI on and off; finally a remote KVM session is opened and `ipmitool chassis identify` is issued before another visual/WebUI observation. The exact source wording, internal Script reference and contradictory Criteria are preserved.
manual_activity: Only after correction, a qualified operator confirms the chassis identity, presses the physical UID button, directly observes color/steady/flash/off behavior, and confirms final restoration. WebUI/KVM/IPMI actions may be command-assisted but require attended visual correlation.
required_inputs: Engineer-corrected Criteria 4 stating whether it belongs to WebUI off and the required physical plus WebUI result
Engineer decision whether KVM session establishment, `chassis identify`, or separate checkpoints cause the flashing state, including priority if controls overlap
Per-control baseline, action, physical LED state, WebUI state, KVM representation, flash frequency/duty/duration or identify timeout, and final state matrix
Chassis/UID button/LED location, blue appearance tolerance, BMC/WebUI/KVM/IPMI versions and exact verified BMC-to-physical-system identity
Approved internal Script revision/content, protected credential path, bounded identify/disable syntax, audit/event expectations and final-off recovery
safety_requirements: Do not execute any control path while Criteria 3 and 4 require opposite physical/WebUI results for the same WebUI-on action.
Do not combine KVM establishment and IPMI identify into one phase until engineering identifies the causal trigger; observe and restore each independently if both remain required.
Verify the target BMC by immutable chassis/serial/location evidence and an attended operator before any WebUI, KVM or IPMI control; stop on any wrong-chassis indication.
Physical button press and LED color/flash observation are operator-only. Command/UI success cannot prove physical appearance or synchronization.
Use protected credentials and a reviewed bounded identify behavior; do not paste secrets into command history or assume an indefinite identify can be safely left active.
Preserve pre-state/audit evidence. After every approved phase, return UID to the defined idle/off state and verify both physical and WebUI views before proceeding.
Stop on stuck on/flash, physical/WebUI disagreement, loss of BMC/KVM access or unexpected audit/event behavior. Restore through the verified path and do not retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: While blocked, only compare source/history and validate a proposed corrected state matrix and Script/package offline; do not control a DUT.
After engineer resolution and approval, capture redacted WebUI/KVM/IPMI action timestamps, returned state, BMC audit/events and engineer-supplied physical evidence for each isolated control path.
Report physical button on/off, WebUI on, WebUI off, KVM-only if applicable and identify-only if applicable as distinct checkpoints with explicit predecessor and restored state.
Do not press hardware, open KVM or WebUI, issue identify, expose credentials, infer physical color from remote state, auto-retry or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Correct the WebUI off/on contradiction and decide the authoritative KVM-versus-identify flashing semantics without modifying the Master Source.
Approve the version-specific control/state/timeout matrix, internal Script applicability, target-identity check, protected access and restore path.
Perform/supervise all physical and remote controls, confirm physical/WebUI synchronization and final idle state, and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The visual limitation is real, but treating the whole case as non-runnable misses the WebUI/IPMI control surfaces and, more importantly, the unresolved acceptance conflict.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No DUT command is recommended while blocked. After resolution, use only the engineer-approved bounded identify/disable form and protected authentication, with operator observation; the Master `ipmitool chassis identify` text remains preserved as the original path.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All manual, WebUI, KVM and IPMI steps, both contradictory Criteria, Script URL and 20/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Approve an action/state table; establish chassis identity and idle baseline; exercise and restore physical button, WebUI on and WebUI off separately; isolate KVM-only and bounded identify-only phases if both are required; correlate physical/WebUI/KVM/audit evidence; finish in verified idle/off state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact chassis UID hardware and versioned BMC WebUI, KVM and IPMI implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/board revision, BMC firmware/WebUI/KVM build, ipmitool version and reviewed Script revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor UID button/LED state machine, WebUI/KVM behavior, IPMI identify semantics and Project correction approval.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates each control cause and makes state priority, timing and recovery explicit, but cannot select the correct conflicting state without engineering ownership.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Testing only visual button toggles omits WebUI, KVM and IPMI synchronization; command success without optical evidence omits the physical UID circuit and appearance.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Corrected state matrix and flash cause, target mapping, versions, timeout and restore approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An unverified target can identify the wrong chassis; overlapping controls can obscure which interface caused or cleared the visible state.

project_override_considerations: A Project Override may document the approved correction and interface-specific behavior, but must cite engineer ownership, preserve both original contradictory statements and report any unsupported KVM or IPMI phase as N/A/untested rather than silently deleting coverage.
expected_evidence: Preserved Master source plus engineer-approved correction for Criteria 4 and explicit KVM/identify flash-trigger decision
Versioned per-control state/priority/timeout matrix, physical UID locator and immutable BMC-to-chassis identity
For physical-button on and off: action timestamp, physical steady-blue/off media, synchronized WebUI state and audit/event evidence
For WebUI on and off: redacted action/state evidence, physical steady-blue/off media, timing and return-to-idle result
Separate KVM-only and bounded identify-only records if applicable, with physical/WebUI/KVM flash behavior, duration/timeout and causal isolation
Final physical/WebUI idle/off proof, no stuck indication or wrong-target action, preserved logs, scope gaps and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Criteria 3 and 4 assign bright-blue and OFF outcomes to the identical `turning on by BMC web control` action. In addition, Procedure performs KVM login and `chassis identify` before one observation while Criteria attribute flashing only to `remote the system`, leaving the causal operation unresolved. These affect the core action-to-result contract and cannot be safely chosen by AI.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A single WebUI-on transition cannot satisfy opposite steady states, and the flashing checkpoint cannot be attributed to KVM or IPMI from the source. Execution would produce unauditable evidence and could test the wrong behavior; engineering correction is required before readiness inputs can make the case executable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Preserves its physical observation boundary but rejects NO as a sufficient disposition because the control paths and source conflict require explicit treatment.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and adds causal isolation of KVM versus IPMI identify, per-phase restore and Script revision review.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Corrects its failure to react to the quoted contradictory Criteria and its omission of remote control semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Confirms the WebUI conflict and extends it with the unresolved flashing cause rather than copying a simple on/off correction assumption.

review_improvement: Prevents two false conclusions: calling either outcome PASS for the same WebUI action, and crediting a flashing observation to KVM when the immediately following identify command may be the actual cause.
independent_technical_reasoning: UID testing is a state-machine and synchronization problem, not only a visual check. Each controller must have an unambiguous transition, visible result, priority and recovery. Here the canonical acceptance assigns two results to one transition and merges two possible flash triggers. Because those are core semantics rather than missing Project values, BLOCKED with engineer-decision ownership is required under V3.1.
